html:
The Akkadian Empire was a kingdom founded by Sargon of Akkad around 2334 BCE that united the cities of Mesopotamia under one ruler for the first time. It is often called the first empire in history. Its dates follow the Middle Chronology; other dating schemes move them by up to a century.

Sargon is said to have started as cupbearer to the king of Kish. He defeated the king who led the Sumerian cities and took them all. He built a new capital, Akkad, whose ruins have never been found. His armies raided as far as Syria and into Elam in Iran.

  • The Akkadians spoke a Semitic language, Akkadian, related to later Hebrew and Arabic. It became the main written language of Mesopotamia, using cuneiform.
  • Sargon's daughter Enheduanna, high priestess at Ur, wrote hymns and is the first author in history known by name.
  • His grandson Naram-Sin called himself "king of the four quarters" of the world and was worshipped as a god in his lifetime.

The empire was hard to hold. Cities revolted again and again. Around 2154 BCE it collapsed, under raids by the Gutians from the Zagros mountains and perhaps a long drought. Later Mesopotamians remembered Sargon as the model of a great king and told legends about him for two thousand years. After a time of disorder, the Ur III dynasty rebuilt a united state in the south.
